headline: BUNKER HILL + SILVER47 CLOSE DEAL — 388M Oz 'Made in America' Silver Producer Born; Bunker Hill Silver Corp Debuts Monday
snippet: Bunker Hill Mining and Silver47 Exploration formally closed their court-approved merger on November 6, creating a combined U.S. silver and critical minerals producer with approximately 388 million silver-equivalent ounces across four projects in Idaho, Nevada, Alaska, and New Mexico. Former Bunker Hill shareholders hold roughly 57% of the 83.7 million combined shares; former Silver47 holders receive 43% via a 0.1724 Bunker Hill share per Silver47 share exchange. The renamed Bunker Hill Silver Corp. is positioning as the largest domestically owned silver platform in the United States at a time when Washington formally lists silver as a critical mineral — and silver spot holds above $52.

headline: MP MATERIALS: GM MAGNETS ARE GO — Q3 Revenue $155.8M, NdPr Output +41%; First Saleable GM Deliveries Start Q4
snippet: MP Materials reported Q3 2026 results on November 5, posting $155.8 million in consolidated revenue and PPA income as NdPr production surged 41% year-over-year to 1,018 metric tonnes and NdPr sales rose 94%. Most significantly, CEO James Litinsky confirmed the company completed General Motors' magnet qualification process — with saleable deliveries to GM and commercial magnet revenue beginning in Q4 2026 — marking the first time a U.S. company has shipped domestic NdPr permanent magnets to a major auto OEM at commercial scale and validating the entire Western rare earth processing buildout.

headline: SUNSHINE SILVER ENDS 50,000m CAMPAIGN — Bonanza Grades Top 7,069 Gpt Ag in NY Boy Vein; Idaho Mine Reboot Eyes 2027 Feasibility
source_name: Sunshine Silver Mining / Junior Mining Network
snippet: Sunshine Silver Mining & Refining (NYSE: SSMR) completed its 50,000-metre underground infill drill program at the historic Sunshine Mine in Idaho's Silver Valley, announcing multiple vein intercepts exceeding 1,000 grams per tonne silver — including 7,069 gpt Ag (7,632 gpt AgEq) over 1.0 metre in the NY Boy Vein. The drill campaign converts inferred resources to higher-confidence categories ahead of a 2027 feasibility study, with management targeting a return to production in late 2028 as one of North America's largest primary silver mines in a metal now on the U.S. critical minerals list.

headline: STANDARD LITHIUM + EQUINOR: ARKANSAS BILLION-DOLLAR BET IMMINENT — $1.45B SW Arkansas FID Due Year-End After Final Hurdles Clear
snippet: Standard Lithium and its Equinor joint venture confirmed that the South West Arkansas direct lithium extraction project has cleared all remaining pre-FID milestones — including NEPA environmental approval and binding offtake agreements with Trafigura and LG Energy Solution covering more than 40% of planned 22,500 tonne-per-annum output — with a final investment decision on the $1.45 billion facility expected before year-end 2026. If taken, the FID would trigger construction of the first large-scale lithium producer in the Smackover Formation, adding a potentially pivotal U.S. domestic supply source as automakers accelerate battery localisation.

headline: U.S. SOUTH EYES REE DOMINANCE — Louisiana Drawing 3 Rare Earth Processors as Domestic Supply Chain Bypasses China
snippet: A Northern Miner investigation published November 6 details how the U.S. South — particularly Louisiana, with its deepwater ports, existing chemical plant infrastructure, and proximity to ionic clay REE deposits — is emerging as the most viable hub for a domestic American rare earth processing supply chain. Three separate rare earth processing ventures are in various stages of development in Louisiana alone, drawing comparisons to the region's petrochemical industry model and offering a potential counter to China's 90% share of global rare earth separation and refining that policymakers say cannot be replicated by a single mine elsewhere.

headline: WASHINGTON WOOS MYANMAR JUNTA FOR RARE EARTHS — Bountiful Deposits Become Pawn in U.S.-China Critical Minerals War
snippet: The U.S. government is actively pursuing deeper diplomatic engagement with Myanmar's military-backed government specifically to unlock access to the country's large and largely untapped heavy rare earth deposits — including dysprosium and terbium critical for defence applications and EV motors. Analysts describe the move as a direct counter-strategy to China's dominant critical minerals position, though it pits supply-chain security directly against human-rights concerns. Myanmar's rare earth deposits are estimated among the largest in Southeast Asia, and a formal U.S. engagement would represent the most significant Western critical minerals diplomacy in the region.

headline: BEIJING'S OVERSEAS MINE RUSH — Agencies, Banks Mobilized to Lock In Global Critical Mineral Supply Chains
snippet: CNBC reporting from November 4 reveals that China has mobilized multiple government agencies, ministries, and state-backed policy banks in a coordinated drive to acquire overseas mining stakes in rare earths, lithium, cobalt, and copper — tightening its grip on critical mineral supply chains even as Western nations scramble to build alternatives. The report notes China already controls approximately 90% of global rare earth separation and processing, and the latest push extends to downstream refining and permanent magnet manufacturing, leaving Western defence and EV industries with no short-term substitute if the November 10 export control pause expires without a durable bilateral arrangement.

headline: COPPER FIGHTS BACK AT $14,000 — China Physical Demand Surge Outweighs Post-Midterm Paper Selloff; LME Bears Squeezed
snippet: LME three-month copper reclaimed the $14,000 per tonne level on November 6 as surging Chinese physical demand — evidenced by record domestic spot premiums — offset post-midterm macro selling pressure that had pushed the metal to multi-month lows near $13,768. The rebound underscores the structural supply-demand tension: Chinese buyers are drawing down physical copper at record premiums while Western investors trim paper exposure, a disconnect that copper bulls argue will ultimately resolve higher as Chinese seasonal restocking accelerates into year-end and Kamoa-Kakula's downgrade further constrains supply growth.

headline: NICKEL SPIKES TO 5-WEEK HIGH — Indonesian Output Crackdown Squeezes Supply; Copper Hits 3-Month Low as Metals Diverge
snippet: Nickel surged to a five-week high on the LME after Indonesia's government signalled tighter enforcement of RKAB ore quotas and potential forced output cuts at major laterite mines — a supply-restriction playbook Jakarta has used repeatedly to shock LME positioning. The move created a rare divergence with copper, which fell to a three-month low on broader macro selling, illustrating how differently the two metals are responding to the same post-midterm macro environment. Battery metal investors are watching whether Indonesia's assertive resource sovereignty stance will extend beyond nickel to cobalt and other EV-critical metals.

headline: RUSSIA'S QUIET URANIUM EMPIRE — Pentagon-Linked Report: Moscow Controls Far More Global Uranium Than Production Data Shows
snippet: A Washington Times analysis of a London-based think tank report published November 5 warns that Russia's true position in global uranium mining and enrichment is substantially greater than published production figures suggest, encompassing state-funded equity stakes in mines from Kazakhstan to Niger and contracted enrichment commitments that give Rosatom unacknowledged pricing and supply leverage over Western utilities. The report argues the uranium junior boom in North America and Africa — while real — is structurally insufficient to displace Russia's entrenched position before 2032, adding urgency to the case for Western governments to accelerate permitting of domestic ISR projects.

headline: URANIUM ONE ENTERS PARAGUAY — 90,000 Ha Yuty ISR Exploration Begins Adjacent to UEC's 896M Lb Resource
snippet: Uranium One Mining (CNSX: UUU) has launched its inaugural exploration program at the 90,000-hectare Yuty Prometeo–San Jose ISR uranium project in Paraguay's Paraná Basin, following receipt of a prospection permit from the country's Vice Ministry of Mining and Energy. The property sits immediately adjacent to Uranium Energy Corp.'s Yuty deposit — estimated at approximately 896 million pounds U3O8 and the largest uranium resource in the Americas outside the Athabasca Basin — giving the small CNSX-listed junior meaningful geological validation and a potential off-take or joint venture pathway as spot uranium trades near US$92 per pound.

headline: SILVER BUCKS THE SELLOFF — $52 White Metal Up 0.68% as Gold Slips; Industrial Demand Narrows Gold-Silver Ratio to 78
snippet: Spot silver rose to approximately $52.03 per ounce on November 6 — up $0.35 or 0.68% on the day — in direct contrast to gold's $39 decline on the stronger-than-expected October payrolls report. The divergence narrowed the gold-silver ratio to 78.24, with analysts noting that persistent industrial demand from solar panel manufacturers and electrical equipment makers is partly insulating silver from pure monetary-driven headwinds. The Silver Institute's 2026 forecast projects a fresh structural supply deficit of approximately 150 million ounces, underpinning silver's resilience at a price level nearly 100% above its year-ago range.
